1.pericope_label: Praise ye the LORD. I will praise the LORD with my whole heart

debates.q: Does the opening Hallelujah belong to the psalm?

sides.view: No — the alphabetical arrangement begins only with the words that follow
It is the title, and the acrostic itself shows why it cannot be part of the body
The psalm has no title unless this word is one

debates.q: What does it mean that the works are sought out?

sides.view: Investigated by the philosopher and lover of nature who traces the First Cause through them
The object of meditation and enquiry — historical proofs first, but the words range wider
Diligent meditation on works from creation to grace

outliers.view: Declares the received division of the psalm into verses improper, since Hebrew poetry requires each hemistich to stand alone with a complete sense
Illustrates a verse of the psalter from a living critic’s campaign against insensibility to natural beauty

4.pericope_label: He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: the LORD is gracious

debates.q: How are the wonderful works made to be remembered?

sides.view: By a memorial made for them — so the Hebrew literally runs
By institutions: the passover, the pot of manna, the supper
By their own construction, which strikes the imagination and edifies the intellect

debates.q: What is the meat given to them that fear him?

sides.view: Simply food; no allusion to spoil is needed, though the next verse makes it probable
Prey — game taken in hunting, or spoil taken from enemies, or the quails
The spoil of Egypt or the manna, and beyond them spiritual food
All necessary provision for being and well-being

outliers.view: Grounds the memorability of God’s works in their aesthetic construction — framed to strike the imagination, interest the senses and charm the intellect

7.pericope_label: The works of his hands are verity and judgment; all his commandments are sure

debates.q: Is reverend a fit rendering of the divine name?

sides.view: No — the Hebrew means terrible, and the English word has become an empty clerical title
It carries three senses at once: terrible, venerable and holy

debates.q: What is the good understanding of the last verse?

sides.view: Good discernment to the doers — the words our version supplies are unnecessary
A good estimation: righteousness wins esteem, and the enduring praise is the good man’s
Obedience as the proof of sound judgment; practical godliness is the test
The chief of wisdom rather than merely its beginning

outliers.view: Uses the verse to attack the title reverend as an empty form of ecclesiastical respect, and denies it belongs to man at all
